state.goal: Recommend only the essential pipeline for CanLang's initial Cloudflare-managed application release. Its foremost objective is adoption, supported by short AI-generated source and a single supported mechanism for each SaaS primitive. Existing generic technology should be reused; recreating UTF-8 machinery conflicts with the user's instruction. The authorized activity is analysis, with implementation of the compiler, platform machinery and library postponed.
state.status: Current artifacts comprise 44 .can examples, Python grammar parsing and twenty manually drafted JS application targets, including CanCRM; their UI revisions remain in progress. Shared dependencies, semantic compilation and canonical execution services are unimplemented. The app path is .can directly to workerd JavaScript ES modules. A future TypeScript-authored standard library would undergo checking and JavaScript emission when that library is released; generated applications must not acquire a TypeScript compilation pass. This consultation chooses no language for implementing the compiler and supplies no reason to replace the existing parser merely for a uniform language.
state.platform: Available Workers facilities include the UTF-8 TextEncoder/TextDecoder APIs and stream variants, JavaScript standard objects, Web Crypto, Intl, streams and HTTP Request/Response/fetch. Cloudflare provisions D1, R2, DO, Queues and email through bindings; running workerd alone does not provision those products. The Node API surface has gaps, and Wrangler can add shims whose methods do not work. Documentation now makes Node compatibility automatic when compatibility_date is at least 2026-08-04, with different opt-in rules for previous dates. Tool and compatibility versions need explicit pinning, and used functions need actual support checks. Evidence: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/web-standards/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/nodejs/ ; https://github.com/cloudflare/workerd
state.packaging: Existing Wrangler capabilities cover esbuild bundling, workerd-aware package exports, local dev, deployment, inspection through dry-run, and compiler-generated configuration. Updating Wrangler can also update its esbuild dependency. Opting into --no-bundle removes Wrangler code processing and its polyfill insertion. A separately pinned esbuild build gives finer direct control over packaging/output, at the cost of providing corresponding module and compatibility integration. Uploads made straight to Cloudflare APIs permit request/dependency control and removal of Wrangler from the path; they require replacement packaging for modules/assets, deployment auth/configuration, resource/update handling and local development/testing integration. No comparative speed result is available. References: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/bundling/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/#generated-wrangler-configuration
state.examples: An inline example must invoke the compiled operation itself, use its independently written expectations, isolate every row, confirm that rejected mutations commit no effects, and keep providers offline. The current @cloudflare/vitest-plugin runs Vitest under workerd with Miniflare and resource bindings. It includes per-file storage separation plus helpers for scheduled events, queues, Durable Object alarms and migrations, but isolating each row still requires generated fixture/reset work. Directly orchestrating workerd with a purpose-built runner removes dependence on Vitest/plugin conventions and can tailor execution to CanLang; it also assigns binding setup, isolation, process control, effect assertions and diagnostics to that runner. Both approaches leave remote provider guarantees, distributed behavior and production latency unproven. Select one automated route rather than adding overlapping simulators or suites. Documentation: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/isolation-and-concurrency/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/test-apis/
state.boundaries: CanLang must own app/import resolution, schema/type/effect checks, CRUD input and default derivation, access-before-query semantics, dependency-aware final invariants, locks evaluated on prior state, bounded operations, exact scalar serialization/storage, replay identity, atomic mutation rules, generated interfaces/views and declared evolution. Candidate MCP, auth, decimal and ICU packages can provide compatible pieces; their availability or native primitives does not establish the language's guarantees. Produced Worker settings, migrations, assets, tests and pinned library dependencies are internal artifacts. Do not demand app-authored wrappers, duplicated entrypoint/dependency inventories or an additional build manifest. Source names cannot supply real credentials, resource identities or provider mappings.

packaging.instructions: Select the first packaging and deployment approach supported by this evidence and the user's goals. Assess each option's control, reused integration and ownership costs, without presenting untested performance or semantic guarantees as facts.

criteria.wrangler_bundle: Generate JavaScript plus compiler-derived settings and other artifacts, and delegate conventional bundling/upload to a pinned Wrangler release. Obtain existing platform and dev integration but depend on Wrangler and its selected esbuild implementation.
criteria.explicit_esbuild: Prepare the final application using a CanLang-controlled pinned esbuild build, then deploy with Wrangler --no-bundle. Retain direct build configuration at the expense of replacing module processing and any compatibility shims that this mode omits.
criteria.api_upload: Package and issue deployment requests against Cloudflare APIs with no central Wrangler dependency. Obtain direct upload and dependency control while arranging equivalent authentication, configuration, resource lifecycle and local execution/testing capabilities.
criteria.unresolved: Postpone adoption of a packaging approach while seeking additional requirements or an observed limitation that separates the available implementations.

examples.instructions: Choose one initial host for automatically running authored examples. Evaluate a maintained workerd test integration and direct dedicated orchestration against operation fidelity, isolation of rows and usable outcomes; no option is a distributed-system proof.

criteria.official_vitest: Lower example tables into Vitest cases using @cloudflare/vitest-plugin, with CanLang-owned fixtures and effect checks. Benefit from supported workerd/resource tooling; retain its dependencies and implement isolation for rows in addition to its storage separation for files.
criteria.custom_workerd: Host emitted examples in a CanLang-specific workerd controller rather than the official Vitest integration. Tailor the execution model and reports while owning process/resource orchestration, isolated rows, effect inspection and failure cleanup.
criteria.unresolved: Hold the test-host decision open because the supplied requirements and documented capabilities are insufficient to justify a first execution route.
